title: PostgreSQL JIT Compilation: Overhead, Thresholds, and OLTP Regressions
realWorldScenario: After upgrading to PostgreSQL 12+, an OLTP payment API experiences random latency spikes where individual queries that normally take 2ms take 120ms. Looking at `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, you see `JIT: Functions: 14, Options: Inlining true, Optimization true, Emission true, Timing: Generation 1.2ms, Inlining 24.5ms, Optimization 62.1ms, Emission 31.8ms`.
questionStatement: Explain PostgreSQL Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation (using LLVM). What does JIT accelerate (expression evaluation, tuple deforming), what causes JIT overhead in OLTP environments, and which configuration parameters control when JIT engages?
expectedConcepts: LLVM native machine code compilation at runtime
Expression evaluation and tuple deforming acceleration
Compilation time overhead (50-200ms) dominating sub-second OLTP queries
OLTP best practice: disable JIT or raise cost threshold
hints: Look at the timing numbers in the scenario: JIT emission took over 110ms alone.
JIT is great for multi-minute OLAP queries, bad for 2ms OLTP queries.
What parameter turns off JIT or raises its cost threshold?
